allowedCidrs.description:
AllowedCIDRs is the inbound client-IP allowlist (IPv4 CIDRs). Pointer so
the service can tell "omitted" (nil -> allow-all default) from an
explicit empty array (block all). Each entry must be a valid IPv4 CIDR;
the list is capped at 50. `dive` validates each element of the slice
(the *[]string + dive form is also used for AllowedCIDRs in UpdateGatewaySpecRequest).

hostAliases.description:
HostAliases is the user-supplied /etc/hosts override list applied to the
gateway pods. Omitted = empty array (no overrides). Each ip must be IPv4
and each hostname a valid RFC-1123 name; capped at 50 entries / 10
hostnames each. ip and hostname uniqueness are enforced in the service.

clientRedirectUris.description:
ClientRedirectURIs is the MCP-client leg redirect_uri allowlist, enforced
at DCR /register and /authorize. Non-loopback entries must be http(s)
URLs; loopback (127.0.0.1/::1/localhost) is auto-allowed at request time
regardless of this list. Whole-object replace on create/PATCH.

iamRequireOwner.description:
IAMRequireOwner toggles owner-binding for Mode=IAM: when on, the caller's
portal account must equal the gateway owner even after OPA allows the
request. Pointer so an absent value resolves to the secure default (on);
send false to opt out and trust OPA alone. Ignored for non-IAM modes.

jwt.description:
JWT is required when mode=JWT (enforced by required_if) and may be
omitted when mode is NONE or IAM. A stale block sent with another
mode is dropped silently — callers toggling modes do not need to
clean up their payload.

idpApp.description:
IdpApp carries the OAuth client at the upstream IdP. ClientSecret is
write-only: it is encrypted server-side and never returned over the wire.
Omit IdpApp to leave any stored IdpApp untouched (preserve-if-absent is
enforced by mergeOrchestratorFields, not here).

mode.description:
swaggertype:"string" suppresses swag's $ref to domain.InboundAuthMode so
the inline enum from `oneof` is the only enum on the property — without
it Swagger UI shows the values twice (once from the $ref, once inline).

privateNetwork.description:
PrivateNetwork is required when networkMode=PRIVATE and must be omitted
(or null) when networkMode=PUBLIC. Enforced by required_if /
excluded_unless binding tags.

publicEndpointEnabled.description:
PublicEndpointEnabled opts a PRIVATE gateway into an internet-reachable
endpoint. Meaningless for PUBLIC (which rejects the whole privateNetwork
block), so it is structurally PRIVATE-only.

routes.description:
Routes is an optional list of IPv4 CIDRs (e.g. "172.16.0.0/12") that the
kube-worker will program as node routes inside the PRIVATE gateway's pod
network. Each entry must be a valid IPv4 CIDR (IPv6 is rejected at the
binding layer). The hard cap of 50 entries is enforced here; semantic
checks (overlap, vs admin/user VPC CIDR) run in the service / saga layer.

subnetId.description: SubnetID is a subnet within the referenced VPC.

vpcId.description: VPCID is a VServer VPC identifier owned by the caller.

targets.description:
Targets count cap is enforced in the service layer against the
operator-configurable gateway.maxTargets — DTO stays shape-level only
per the type doc above. `dive` still validates each element.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint must be an absolute http:// or https:// URL (hostname or
IP:port host both accepted). The scheme is mandatory — a bare
host[:port] is rejected so callers state the protocol explicitly.
URL shape and length cap are enforced by domain.Target.Validate()
in the service layer.

allowedCidrs.description:
AllowedCIDRs uses JSON Merge Patch semantics: absent (nil) = no-op,
a present array replaces the stored allowlist. An explicit empty array
means block all client IPs. Each entry must be a valid IPv4 CIDR (max 50).

displayName.description:
DisplayName and Description: nil (absent / null) preserves the stored
value; a non-nil pointer replaces — pass "" to clear, any non-empty
value to set. Format checks (length + charset) on non-empty values run
inline in the handler. Swagger renders them as strings with x-nullable.

hostAliases.description:
HostAliases uses whole-list replace semantics: absent (nil) = no-op, a
present array replaces the stored list (explicit [] = clear all
overrides). Validation matches CreateGatewayRequest.

clientRedirectUris.description:
ClientRedirectURIs is the MCP-client leg redirect_uri allowlist, enforced
at DCR /register and /authorize. Non-loopback entries must be http(s)
URLs; loopback (127.0.0.1/::1/localhost) is auto-allowed at request time
regardless of this list. Whole-object replace on create/PATCH.

IAMRequireOwner toggles owner-binding for Mode=IAM: when on, the caller's
portal account must equal the gateway owner even after OPA allows the
request. Pointer so an absent value resolves to the secure default (on);
send false to opt out and trust OPA alone. Ignored for non-IAM modes.

omitted when mode is NONE or IAM. A stale block sent with another
mode is dropped silently — callers toggling modes do not need to
clean up their payload.

Omit IdpApp to leave any stored IdpApp untouched (preserve-if-absent is

mode.description:
swaggertype:"string" suppresses swag's $ref to domain.InboundAuthMode so
the inline enum from `oneof` is the only enum on the property — without

policyGroupId.description:
PolicyGroupID uses JSON Merge Patch semantics: absent = no-op,
JSON null = clear, non-empty string = set. The binding tag is bypassed
because Nullable[string] is not a string; format (refid + length)
and the rejection of empty strings are enforced in the handler before
the service is called. Swagger renders it as a string for the
happy-path documentation.

privateNetwork.description:
PrivateNetwork is the PRIVATE-only mutable block (block-replace; both
sub-fields required when present). Omit to leave routes + toggle alone.

targets.description:
Targets count cap is enforced in the service layer against the
operator-configurable gateway.maxTargets (see CreateGatewayRequest).

endpoint.description:
Endpoint must be an absolute http:// or https:// URL (hostname or
IP:port host both accepted). The scheme is mandatory — a bare
host[:port] is rejected so callers state the protocol explicitly.
URL shape and length cap are enforced by domain.Target.Validate()
in the service layer.

name.description: Name of the memory store, for the caller to recognise it by.

description.description: What this memory store is for. May be empty, but has to be present.
description.example: Memory for my customer support chatbot

eventExpiryDuration.description: How many days raw events are retained, between 1 and 365. Events older than this are left out of event listings and are deleted by a background job. Memory records extracted from them are not affected.

longTermMemoryStrategies.description: The long-term memory strategies to attach to this memory, at most 10. Each one governs what kind of facts are extracted from the events and which namespace the resulting memory records are stored under. Two strategies of the same `type` cannot be attached to the same memory.

name.description: Name of the strategy, for the caller to recognise it by.

type.description: Which kind of facts to extract. Has to be one of the built-in strategy types: `USER_PREFERENCES` for the preferences, habits and traits of the user, `SEMANTIC` for general factual statements, or `CUSTOM` to drive extraction with your own `customFactExtractionPrompt` instead.

customFactExtractionPrompt.description: Your own fact extraction instructions, used in place of the built-in prompt. Only meaningful when `type` is `CUSTOM`.
customFactExtractionPrompt.example: Extract only facts related to the user's technical stack and project requirements.

namespaceTemplate.description: Where the extracted memory records are stored, as a template. The placeholders `{memoryStrategyId}`, `{actorId}` and `{sessionId}` are substituted at extraction time, and the resolved string is the `namespace` to pass when listing or searching records. Choosing which placeholders to include is what scopes the records: `{actorId}` alone makes them shared across all of that actor's sessions, adding `{sessionId}` confines them to one session.

enableAutomaticMemoryRecordGeneration.description: Whether a background job runs this strategy over new events on its own schedule. When false, records are only extracted when you call one of the `memory-records:generate-from-...` endpoints.

query.description: What to search for. Matching is by semantic similarity rather than keyword, so phrase this as the question the agent needs answered.
query.example: What are this user's UI preferences?

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return, between 5 and 200.

scoreThreshold.description: Minimum similarity score a record has to reach to be returned, between 0 and 1. Defaults to 0, which returns the `limit` closest records however weak the match. Raise it to trade recall for precision.

memoryRecords.description: The facts to store, at most 100, each a self-contained sentence as the extraction pipeline would have produced. They are stored verbatim under the given namespace and are searchable straight away.

operations.summary: Generate memory records from a session

chatMessages.description: The conversation to extract facts from, at most 100 messages, in chronological order. These are read for extraction only and are not stored as events, so they will not appear in event listings afterwards.

content.example: I prefer dark mode and short answers.

payload.description: The content of the event. Which fields apply depends on `payload.type`.

type.description: What kind of event this is. `conversational` for a text turn, which requires `role` and `message`, or `binary` for arbitrary content, which requires `binaryData`. Only long-term memory strategies read conversational events, so binary events are stored and returned but never contribute to memory records.

role.description: Who produced the message: `user`, `assistant` or `system`. Required when `type` is `conversational`, and ignored otherwise.

message.description: The text of the turn. Required when `type` is `conversational`, and ignored otherwise.
message.example: I prefer dark mode and short answers.

binaryData.description: Arbitrary content, base64-encoded. Required when `type` is `binary`, and ignored otherwise.

eventTimestamp.description: When the interaction happened, as an ISO-8601 instant in UTC. Defaults to the time the request is received. Set it explicitly when replaying or backfilling a conversation, since this is the timestamp events are ordered, filtered and expired by.

body.description: The configuration of a new OpenClaw instance. Every field is optional; an omitted one falls back to the platform default.

name.description: Name of the instance. Defaults to the generated instance id.

versionId.description: Id of the published OpenClaw version to run, from `GET /v1/openclaw-versions`. Defaults to the version marked default in that catalog.

greenNodeModelProvider.description: Whether the instance calls models through GreenNode MaaS. When enabled the platform provisions a MaaS API key and points the instance at it; when disabled the agent must reach its own model provider. Defaults to disabled.

enabled.description: Turns the GreenNode model provider on. When false no MaaS key is provisioned and the agent must call its own provider.

apiKeyName.description: Name of one of your existing MaaS API keys to call models with; the key must already exist and be active. Omit it to use the platform-managed `openclaw-service` key, which is created for you if it does not exist yet. Ignored when `enabled` is false.

environmentVariables.description: Environment variables set on the OpenClaw container.

channels.description: Messaging channels the instance talks to users on. Omit to create an instance with no channel connected.

telegram.description: Telegram bot the instance answers on.

botToken.description: Token of the bot the instance runs as, issued by the messaging platform.

dmPolicy.description: Who may direct-message the bot. `allowlist` restricts it to the users listed in `dmAllowedUserIds`; `pairing` instead has users pair themselves with the bot. Required whenever the channel is configured.

zalo.description: Zalo bot the instance answers on.

botToken.description: Token of the bot the instance runs as, issued by the messaging platform.

dmPolicy.description: Who may direct-message the bot. `allowlist` restricts it to the users listed in `dmAllowedUserIds`; `pairing` instead has users pair themselves with the bot. Required whenever the channel is configured.

flavorId.description: Id of the compute flavor the instance runs on, from `GET /v1/flavors?resourceType=openclaw`. Defaults to the first flavor in that list.

poc.description: Whether to create the instance against the account's proof-of-concept quota instead of its paid quota. Only accounts enabled for PoC may set this.

body.description: Which slice of the log stream to return: the time range to look in, an optional full-text filter, and where in the result set to start.

from.description: Number of matching records to skip before the returned page — an offset, not a page number.

fromTimestamp.description: Only return records at or after this instant, as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp. Omit for no lower bound.

toTimestamp.description: Only return records at or before this instant, as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp. Omit for no upper bound.

query.description: Only return records whose message contains this phrase. Omit to return every record in the range.

order.description: Sort direction on the record timestamp, newest first (`desc`) or oldest first (`asc`). Case-insensitive; defaults to `desc`.

body.description: Which version of the runtime to deploy as a new endpoint, and what to call it.

name.description: Name of the endpoint. Must be unique within the runtime, which in practice rules out `DEFAULT`: that endpoint is created with the runtime and tracks its latest version.

version.description: Runtime version this endpoint serves, from `GET /v1/agent-runtimes/{id}/versions`. Unlike the DEFAULT endpoint, it stays pinned here until you change it explicitly.

body.description: The configuration of a runtime version. Every update writes these values into a new immutable version and rolls the DEFAULT endpoint onto it.

description.description: Free-form description of what the agent does. Must be present, but may be an empty string.

imageUrl.description: Reference of the container image the agent runs from, in Docker `[registry/]repository[:tag|@digest]` form. The registry must be reachable from the public internet: an image whose registry host resolves to a private or internal address is rejected.

imageAuth.description: Credentials used to pull the image. Must be present; send it with `enabled: false` for an image that needs no authentication.

enabled.description: Whether the image needs credentials to pull. When false the rest of this object is ignored.

useAgentBaseRegistryCredentials.description: Pull the image with the platform's own AgentBase registry credentials instead of `username`/`password`. Only accepted when the image lives in the AgentBase registry.

username.description: Registry username. Required when `enabled` is true and `useAgentBaseRegistryCredentials` is false.

password.description: Registry password or access token. Required when `enabled` is true and `useAgentBaseRegistryCredentials` is false. Stored encrypted and never returned by the API.

environmentVariables.description: Environment variables set on the agent container. Names the platform injects itself (the `GREENNODE_*` and `OTEL_*` variables) are reserved and rejected, since an injected value would otherwise silently replace yours.

networkConfig.description: Where the endpoints of this runtime are reachable from. Omit for a public endpoint.

mode.description: PUBLIC exposes the endpoints on the internet. VPC places them inside one of your VPCs, reachable only from that network; VPC mode does not support `allowedCidrs` or inbound auth.

vpcId.description: Id of the VPC the endpoints are placed in. Required in VPC mode; the VPC must have DNS enabled.

subnetId.description: Id of the subnet within `vpcId` the endpoints are placed in. Required in VPC mode.

inboundAuth.description: How requests reaching the endpoints are authenticated. Omit to leave the endpoints unauthenticated (mode NONE). Only supported in PUBLIC network mode.

mode.description: NONE lets every request through. IAM requires a VNG Cloud IAM token belonging to the account that owns the endpoint. JWT verifies a bearer token issued by your own identity provider, configured under `jwt`.

jwt.description: Identity provider settings used to verify inbound bearer tokens. Required when `mode` is JWT, and ignored otherwise.

source.description: Where the signing keys come from. DISCOVERY fetches them from the provider's metadata document at `discoveryUrl`. JWKS uses the key set pasted into `jwks`, for a provider the platform cannot reach. The field the other source does not use is dropped.

jwks.description: Public JSON Web Key Set used to verify token signatures, as an RFC 7517 `{"keys": [...]}` document. Required when `source` is JWKS. Must be at most 32 KiB and 10 keys, and must contain public keys only — a key carrying private material is rejected.

discoveryUrl.description: URL of the provider's metadata document. Required when `source` is DISCOVERY. Must be https, must not resolve to a private or internal address, and must end with `/.well-known/openid-configuration` or `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` so the issuer can be derived from it.

principalClaim.description: Claim whose value identifies the caller and is forwarded to the agent. Defaults to `sub`.

protocol.description: Wire protocol the agent speaks. MCP makes the endpoint answer authentication failures with the MCP error envelope and the OAuth discovery hint instead of a plain HTTP status. Defaults to HTTP.

flavorId.description: Id of the compute flavor the endpoints run on, from `GET /v1/flavors`. The flavor must be enabled and must support the resource type of the chosen network mode (`agent-runtime` for PUBLIC, `agent-runtime-vpc` for VPC).

autoscaling.description: How the endpoints scale under load. Required.

maxReplicas.description: Largest number of replicas an endpoint may scale up to.

cpuUtilization.description: Average CPU utilization, as a percentage, that triggers scaling out.

memoryUtilization.description: Average memory utilization, as a percentage, that triggers scaling out.
